name: Sandpiper utterance export · SYNTHETIC
description: SYNTHETIC sample only. Sandpiper (National Tutoring Observatory) PER_UTTERANCE utterances CSV: each utterance is an observed dialogue turn, and annotation codes are kept as inferred assertions by their annotator, never as help.

mapping.identifier_handling: session_id is HMAC-pseudonymized as the record subject and kept as text in each utterance and activity; Sandpiper exports carry no learner identifier. Utterance text is kept. This is not a general anonymizer.
mapping.order: sequence_id as a positive integer string, unique within a session

subjectScope: adapter + session_id + tenant + key; a session pseudonym, not a learner

source.license: MIT (Sandpiper documentation examples, Copyright (c) 2025 National Tutoring Observatory; arrangement by QLM, MIT)
source.citation: Utterances and the one annotation are Sandpiper's own documented examples (documentation/transcripts.md and documentation/schemas/examples/transcript-per-utterance.json at the pinned revision), arranged by QLM in the PER_UTTERANCE utterances-CSV layout written by app/functions/outputRunDataToCSV/app.ts. Not National Tutoring Observatory data and not a real Sandpiper export.
source.selectionNote: Eight documented example utterances in two sessions: session_001 (six utterances with documented start/end times and one AI annotation, given_praise = Great!) and session_002 (two utterances from the CSV upload example, no times). Annotation columns follow the export's naming for annotator AI-0, slot 0: the prompt field given_praise plus the markedAs and votingReason columns the export always adds. _id values for session_002 follow the 0-based pattern of the documented JSON example.
limitations: SYNTHETIC fixture built from Sandpiper's documentation examples. There is no public National Tutoring Observatory dataset here: no real learner, tutor, session or Sandpiper run export is included or was examined.
The layout follows Sandpiper's export code at the pinned revision. Real exports from other Sandpiper versions may differ, and a matching shape does not authenticate where a file came from.

Annotation codes, from a model or a person, are inferred assertions about an utterance. They are not observations of help being requested, offered, generated, transmitted, displayed or accepted, and no code sets a help stage.
start_time and end_time are kept as the source's unparsed strings (Sandpiper allows any format); an empty cell is kept as null. No clock time is derived.

Sandpiper's run export writes prompt-schema fields plus markedAs and votingReason; it does not write identifiedBy. identifiedBy is kept only when a column carries it, and an annotator name such as AI-0 is kept as given, not read as model or person.
sequence_id must be a positive integer string. Sandpiper's human-annotation template documentation shows sequence_id starting at 0; such files are refused rather than renumbered.
Session-level (PER_SESSION) annotations, the sessions and meta CSVs, prompts and model details are not imported.
source.summary: 2 SYNTHETIC sessions · 8 utterances · 1 inferred annotation code · 0 observed learners
